title: Design System: The Daily Catch · CSCD01

shout.purpose: The LINES IN! cast callout only: red, rotated -15° (-24° on phones), slammed from weight 250 to 900 with a black misregistration.

display.purpose: Verdict name and help title; uppercase, rotated -4 to -6 degrees, slammed from light to 900. On the landscape spread the verdict grows to min(168px, 8.4vw, 15.5dvh) and steps down only as far as its longest word needs.

headline.purpose: Control message on the black band, the masthead and the red "Next to present" overprint.

title.purpose: Boat name tags (up to four lines; 19px in lanes under 130px, up to 30px in lanes over about 490px), plate labels, group names, step titles, the catch-feed line, ledger names and lengths, toasts. The back-row minimum.

lever.purpose: Lever labels; the band CAST lever steps up to 30px.

ui.purpose: Text buttons, crew footer, status tag, spine legend, number blocks (at 900), feed label, PRESENTED and ledger stamps, cast numbers in Today's catch, and the SMALLEST stamp on phones (it grows to 30px on projector screens). Smallest step allowed to carry red with black.

numeral.purpose: Fish lengths, the depth gauge and the crew heading; tabular figures.

numeral-xl.purpose: Help step numerals only: red with a 2px black misregistration.

label.purpose: Eyebrow tags, gauge keys, table headings, the scroll hint; tracked caps.

body.purpose: Explanatory sentences only (help, tips, fairness note, winner sentence), Archivo at 88% width.

shadows.name: plate-drop
shadows.purpose: Resting levers, plates, the ? plate and the Options tag (filter).

shadows.name: plate-drop-hover
shadows.purpose: Hover: plate lifts -2px and the drop extends.

shadows.name: plate-drop-active
shadows.purpose: Press: plate moves +3px and the gap closes.

shadows.name: red-drop
shadows.purpose: Plates on the black band; the open Options tag.

shadows.name: cream-drop
shadows.purpose: The lever on the black band.

shadows.name: stamp-drop
shadows.purpose: The SMALLEST stamp (box-shadow); cream (#f2ede2) once its row inks over, red (#d7261e) under the verdict's number plate.

shadows.name: tick-preview
shadows.purpose: Hovering an Options tick box previews the click (box-shadow).

shadows.name: misregistered-type
shadows.purpose: Red display type over cream (text-shadow); .045em on the cast callout.

motion.name: ease-slam
motion.purpose: Every slam, press and panel transition; overshoot lives in keyframes.

motion.name: ease-shockwave
motion.purpose: The ring behind the cast callout.

motion.name: press
motion.purpose: Plate lift and drop on hover.

motion.name: press-active
motion.purpose: Plate pushed into the page.

motion.name: invert
motion.purpose: Icon, text and add button colour inversions.

motion.name: page-slam
motion.purpose: Dialog rises 26px from -1.5deg and 0.97 scale.

motion.name: shout
motion.purpose: The verdict name, shouted last: scale 2.3 to 1 about its left middle, weight 200 to 900, one overshoot. Its start announces the verdict and plays the finish tone.

motion.name: row-slam
motion.purpose: Result rows slam in from the left in boat order, from 80ms.

motion.name: tape-out
motion.purpose: Bars and fish unroll at one speed along every ruler; each length prints (scale 1.7 to 1, weight 300 to 900) where its tape stops.

motion.name: stamp
motion.purpose: SMALLEST stamps from 2.6× with a twist; on impact the winning row inverts and thumps 4px. Until then it wears the plain print of every row.

motion.name: reveal-order
motion.purpose: Evidence before verdict: rows, tapes and lengths, stamp, then 'Next to present', the name, its fish, and at 1.5s the sentence and actions. Replayed results and reduced motion open finished.

motion.name: dock-hold
motion.value: 900ms after the last landing; hoist 350ms; haul 2.5×
motion.purpose: Once every hook has a fish, remaining catches are reeled home 2.5× faster after their 0.6s struggle. Landed catches swing up to hang head-first from hoisted rods in plain ink, and the board holds before the reveal.

motion.name: cast-slam
motion.purpose: LINES IN callout: scale 2.8 to 1, weight 250 to 900, then flies off.

motion.name: canvas-shout
motion.purpose: Catch shouts: scale 2.2 to 1, weight 300 to 900, loudness 0.8 to 1.2 by catch order; board shake up to 4.5px.

motion.name: status-blink
motion.purpose: The status dot blinks red while fishing; pauses with the round.

motion.name: tail-wake
motion.purpose: Alternating tail beats shed curved ink strokes that spread, thin 1.5 to 0.8px and fade; frozen when paused, omitted under reduced motion.

motion.name: watch-cap
motion.purpose: Playback runs just fast enough that the last bite lands by 16.5s, so the room watches for 20s at most. Presentation only; fishing.js fixes every catch.

motion.name: hooked-pop
motion.purpose: A hooked fish pops to twice its swimming size with one overshoot, holds through the fight and settles to 1.25× as it comes aboard, on the reel's clock, never on its length.

motion.name: hold-stamp
motion.purpose: LINES HELD lands with the SMALLEST stamp's motion when a round is paused; no red.

motion.name: dock-note-in
motion.purpose: The first-run dock note lands after load with the dialogs' page slam.

motion.name: ledger-line
motion.purpose: A new or changed line in Today's catch slams in once the room is back at the dock; its stamp lands 0.3s later. The slip itself never moves.

motion.name: dive-lift
motion.purpose: The masthead and the TA's corner lift off the page as the camera dives (cubic-bezier(.7, 0, .84, 0)) and drop back with the slam curve as it surfaces.

motion.name: toast
motion.value: 280ms rise; offers held 8s (Undo) or 12s (Reveal its catch)
motion.purpose: The ink toast rises 14px into the band message's place, turned -2°.

motion.name: reduced-motion
motion.purpose: prefers-reduced-motion disables all animations, transitions, the cast callout, ambient drift and shake.

components.name: Lever
components.description: The one red action per view that moves the round forward (cast, start, mark presented).
components.css: .ds-lever { --face: var(--red, #d7261e); --fg: var(--ink, #111111); --edge: var(--ink, #111111); --drop: var(--ink, #111111); --slant: 16px; position: relative; isolation: isolate; display: inline-flex; align-items: center; gap: 12px; min-height: 58px; padding: 9px 32px 9px 11px; border: 0; background: none; color: var(--fg); font-family: var(--display, 'Big Shoulders Variable', 'Arial Narrow', Impact, sans-serif); font-weight: 900; font-size: 26px; line-height: 1; text-transform: uppercase; letter-spacing: .03em; white-space: nowrap; cursor: pointer; filter: drop-shadow(4px 4px 0 var(--drop)); transition: transform .14s cubic-bezier(.16,1,.3,1), filter .14s cubic-bezier(.16,1,.3,1); } .ds-lever::before { content: ''; position: absolute; inset: 0; z-index: -2; background: var(--edge); clip-path: polygon(0 0, 100% 0, calc(100% - var(--slant)) 100%, 0 100%); } .ds-lever::after { content: ''; position: absolute; inset: 3px; z-index: -1; background: var(--face); clip-path: polygon(0 0, calc(100% - 1px) 0, calc(100% - var(--slant) + 1px) 100%, 0 100%); } .ds-lever .ds-label { display: inline-block; transform: skewX(-9deg); } .ds-lever:hover { transform: translate(-2px, -2px); filter: drop-shadow(6px 6px 0 var(--drop)); } .ds-lever:active { transform: translate(3px, 3px); filter: drop-shadow(1px 1px 0 var(--drop)); transition-duration: .05s; } .ds-lever:focus-visible { outline: 3px solid var(--red, #d7261e); outline-offset: 4px; } .ds-lever:hover { --fg: var(--stock, #f2ede2); }

components.name: Plate Button
components.description: Secondary bolted plate; inverts to black on hover.

components.description: Frameless caps action; turns red and underlines on hover.

components.name: Crew Row
components.description: Ruled ledger line with a wood-type number block and a borderless name input.
components.css: .ds-crew-row { display: flex; align-items: center; gap: 10px; min-height: 46px; width: 320px; border-top: 3px solid var(--ink, #111111); border-bottom: 1px solid var(--ink, #111111); background: var(--stock, #f2ede2); transition: background .12s; } .ds-crew-row:focus-within { background: var(--stock-2, #e7dfcd); box-shadow: inset 0 -3px var(--red, #d7261e); } .ds-number { display: grid; place-items: center; width: 34px; height: 34px; background: var(--ink, #111111); color: var(--stock, #f2ede2); font: 900 19px/1 var(--display, 'Big Shoulders Variable', 'Arial Narrow', Impact, sans-serif); font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums; } .ds-crew-row input { flex: 1; min-width: 0; padding: 8px 0; border: 0; background: transparent; color: var(--ink, #111111); font-family: var(--text, 'Archivo Variable', 'Arial Narrow', Arial, sans-serif); font-size: 16px; font-weight: 600; font-stretch: 85%; } .ds-crew-row input:focus { outline: none; }

components.name: Options Tag
components.description: The TA's corner, beside the ? plate that opens How to play: a slanted plate that inverts with a red drop when open.

components.name: Eyebrow Tag
components.description: Black slab label that opens headings and dialogs.
components.css: .ds-eyebrow { display: inline-block; margin: 0; padding: 6px 11px 5px; background: var(--ink, #111111); color: var(--stock, #f2ede2); font-family: var(--display, 'Big Shoulders Variable', 'Arial Narrow', Impact, sans-serif); font-size: 14px; font-weight: 800; line-height: 1; letter-spacing: .16em; text-transform: uppercase; }

components.name: Dock Strip Tag
components.description: The board's name tag, one per lane: a black tag led by a paper number plate, wrapping to four lines. It is the TA's Presented toggle; a moored boat's tag turns to a faded outline, struck through and stamped PRESENTED at -5°.

components.name: Clipped Plate
components.description: Framed cream plate with a 45-degree clipped top-right corner (22px panel, 26px dialog, 16px dock note, 14px ledger, 12px depth gauge), used for panels, dialogs, the dock note, Today's catch and the depth gauge.

components.name: To-Scale Haul
components.description: Signature results table: each catch is a measuring bar ending in its fish, drawn to scale over a 10% tick ruler. narrative.overview:
The derby is a machine-bound futurist book: a cream spread fixed to its spine with brushed-aluminium hex bolts, where every bite, catch and verdict is slammed in tilted wood type. The page is one full-bleed print. The sea is engraved as horizontal lines of force that thicken with depth. Boats, fish, hooks and headlands are printed in solid black ink. Controls are riveted plates laid over that print. There is one colour of ink besides black, a mechanical red, and it goes where the pressure is.

The system is built for a projector in a lit tutorial room. That means a cream ground rather than a dark one, heavy ink, and a scale the back row can read: boat names at 22px in tags that fill their lane, hook plates with 25px numerals, fishing lines drawn 2.4 to 3.6px, hooked fish printed at twice their swimming size. Density is low and loud. Few words, set very large, in condensed caps.

Motion is percussive. Type arrives slammed: it lands oversized and light, snaps to full weight, overshoots once and settles. The loudness of a catch follows the order of catches, never the size of the fish, so the animation can never hint at the result. The reveal runs evidence first: the catches hang at the dock, the rows and rulers print, SMALLEST stamps, and only then is the name shouted. Reduced motion turns every slam, shake and drift off. The system rejects two things: the glossy candy-button mobile game and the neon arcade.
keyCharacteristics: Two inks plus red: cream stock, type black, one mechanical red.
Condensed wood-type caps (Big Shoulders) for everything the room reads; Archivo only for explanatory sentences.

Identity by number, not colour: every boat is a two-digit wood-type numeral on its hull, hook plate, name tag, crew row and result row, and the number leads its name wherever the name is printed ("05 · REBASE RANGERS").
Hard offset ink drops and misregistered red-over-black type in place of soft shadows.
Square plates with clipped corners and slanted trailing edges, fastened with bolts.
Tilted, slammed type: fixed rotations between -4° and -15°, weight swinging from 300 to 900.

rules.name: The Two Inks Rule
rules.body: Everything is printed in type black on stock cream, plus red. Group colours (the 12-colour boat set) and fish colours (the 6-colour fish set) stay in data for storage and fairness; they are never rendered. Fish colours become six ink markings instead: solid, bars, spots, scale arcs, split and hatch.

rules.name: The Pressure Red Rule
rules.body: On anything the room reads as data or can act on, red means pressure: the line under strain, the lever to pull, the verdict. Red is never used as a boat's identity, and never for a resting mark. The depth-scale numerals, an idle bobber's cap, a presented boat's stamp, the Options tick box and ready square, and the spine legend all print in ink. The sun family (disc, glitter, lighthouse bands) is the only red scenery, and nothing else on the board may borrow it.

rules.name: The Number Is The Name Rule
rules.body: A boat's identity travels as a two-digit wood-type numeral (01 to 12) on its hull, hook plate, name tag, crew row, result row and verdict. Wherever a name is printed, the number leads it: "05 · REBASE RANGERS" on the band, the catch feed, the catch shout and the toast; a paper number plate at the head of the board's name tags. The fish on the hook never carries identity; the plate does.

rules.name: The Slam Rule
rules.body: Display type arrives oversized and light, snaps to weight 900, overshoots once and settles. The weight change is part of the motion (canvas shouts go 300→900, the cast callout 250→900, the verdict 200→900).

rules.name: The Caps Rule
rules.body: Everything set in Big Shoulders is uppercase. Archivo sentences keep normal case.

rules.name: The Skewed Label Rule
rules.body: Labels inside levers and plates are skewed -9°, so the type leans into the slanted trailing edge.

rules.name: The Hard Drop Rule
rules.body: Every shadow has zero blur and a positive x and y offset. Motion changes the offset; nothing ever fades in a glow.

dos: **Do** print in two inks plus red: type black (#111111) on stock cream (#f2ede2), with mechanical red (#d7261e) only where there is pressure or the printed sun.
**Do** carry group identity as a two-digit wood-type numeral on hull, hook plate, name tag, crew row and result row, and lead every printed name with it.

**Do** set anything the back row reads in Big Shoulders caps at 22px or larger, weight 800–900. The 19px UI step stands in only where the room would otherwise lose a name: lanes under 130px, the compact haul, and phones.
**Do** give raised controls a hard zero-blur ink drop (4px 4px 0) and let press states close the gap.
**Do** use the steep ease-out cubic-bezier(.16, 1, .3, 1) for every slam, and put the overshoot in keyframes, not in the curve.
**Do** tie shout loudness and slam order to catch order, never to fish length.
**Do** switch off every slam, shake, drift and callout under prefers-reduced-motion.
**Do** fasten plates with the brushed-aluminium hex bolt; it is the only place a gradient appears.
donts: **Don't** render the per-group or per-fish colour sets; translate fish colour into one of the six ink markings.
**Don't** make anything glossy, candy-coloured or rounded like a mobile game button, and don't use neon glows or dark arcade grounds.
**Don't** use rounded rectangles; circles are allowed only as printed discs (bolts, sun, bobbers, shockwave rings).
**Don't** use blurred shadows or translucent glass layers over the board.
**Don't** set small body-size text in red on black or black on red; red and ink together hold only about 3.7:1, so red-carried type starts at the 19px UI step at weight 800+ (large text).
**Don't** load fonts or art from the network; fonts are self-hosted and all scene art is drawn in code.
